root_cause: When the #more button is removed from the DOM while focused, the focus trap's checkFocusIn handler attempts to restore focus to the removed node (stored in state.mostRecentlyFocusedNode). The tryFocus function does not verify the node is still in the document, causing focus to remain on body instead of falling back to the initial focus node (#close).
repair_strategy: Modify checkFocusIn to directly request the initial focus node (first tabbable element) when focus escapes, bypassing the potentially stale mostRecentlyFocusedNode. Also harden tryFocus to reject nodes no longer in the document as a safety net.
expected_accessibility_effect: After clicking the #more button (which removes itself), focus will remain trapped inside the dialog on the #close button (the first tabbable node), ensuring keyboard users can continue to navigate the dialog without accidentally leaving it. The Escape key will still close the dialog and return focus to the #open button.
functional_risks: If the initial focus node is also removed from the document, the fallback might fail. However, the trap already requires at least one tabbable node, and we only remove the #more button, which is not the initial focus node (the initial focus node is #close).

The change to checkFocusIn might affect other scenarios where focus escapes to a valid node outside the trap that we'd want to return to, but the trap's purpose is to keep focus inside, so directing to the initial focus node is appropriate.
verification_requirements: After clicking the #more button, pressing Tab should move focus to the #close button (not to the body).
The dialog should retain focus within after the #more button is removed.
The Escape key should still close the dialog and return focus to the #open button.
The initial focus when opening the dialog should remain on the #close button.
